Prompt¶

Using the /okn-bioanalysis workflow, conduct a reproducible, integrative study of spaceflight-induced bone loss across relevant mcp-okn knowledge graphs. Investigate the genetic, molecular, cellular, physiological, and clinical mechanisms underlying bone loss, including associated genes, variants, pathways, biomarkers, therapeutic targets, and countermeasures. Compare findings from actual spaceflight, terrestrial microgravity analogs, and related bone disorders. Identify consensus findings, conflicting evidence, promising therapeutic and drug-repurposing opportunities, and knowledge gaps. Assess evidence strength, cross-graph agreement, and provenance, distinguishing established mechanisms from emerging hypotheses. Present a comprehensive, evidence-backed report using /okn-report-style.

Notes¶

Spaceflight (OSD-690 marrow WT / Nrf2-KO; OSD-546 osteogenic hMSC) and hindlimb-unloading (OSD-467 cortical bone; OSD-214 marrow) DE from spoke-genelab (adj p <= 0.05, |log2FC| >= 1, mouse -> human orthologs), joined on Entrez to rdkg (curated low-BMD rare-disease genes) and digcfdekg (BMD/osteoporosis traits), on HGNC symbol to prokn (GO-BP, Reactome, compound -> target), and via babel to map rdkg osteoporosis drugs to prokn targets. Hypergeometric + BH-FDR against explicit KG universes. Hypothesis generation only.

Re-running this study¶

Every query cell loads the rows the session logged (data/), so the notebook runs offline and shows the original results. To rerun the study from scratch, uncomment # RERUN = True in the next cell and run all cells (or start Jupyter with OKN_RERUN=1): every query is then re-executed live against the OKN federation. Or run the last cell (verify_all()) to compare each query's live result with the logged one. A difference usually means the knowledge graph was redeployed since the study ran, not that the analysis is wrong.

In [1]:
import os

import pandas as pd

from okn_sparql import run_query, verify_all

# By default (RERUN = False) every query cell loads the rows logged during the

# Starting Jupyter with OKN_RERUN=1 sets RERUN = True without editing the notebook.
RERUN = os.environ.get("OKN_RERUN", "") == "1"

SPARQL (12 lines) 
PREFIX rdf: <http://www.w3.org/1999/02/22-rdf-syntax-ns#>
PREFIX kg: <https://purl.org/okn/frink/kg/spoke-genelab/schema/>
SELECT ?gene ?symbol ?taxon ?lfc ?p ?hgene ?hsym WHERE {
  GRAPH <https://purl.org/okn/frink/kg/spoke-genelab> {
    ?st rdf:subject <https://purl.org/okn/frink/kg/spoke-genelab/node/OSD-467-4d3703d7504fd48caceedadb36799194> ;
        rdf:predicate kg:MEASURED_DIFFERENTIAL_EXPRESSION_ASmMG ; rdf:object ?gene ;
        kg:log2fc ?lfc ; kg:adj_p_value ?p .
    FILTER(?p <= 0.05 && ABS(?lfc) >= 1)
    OPTIONAL { ?gene kg:symbol ?symbol } OPTIONAL { ?gene kg:taxonomy ?taxon }
    OPTIONAL { ?gene kg:IS_ORTHOLOG_MGiG ?hgene . OPTIONAL { ?hgene kg:symbol ?hsym } }
  }
}

Runs as queries/sent/q05.rq: the server's result-neutral plan rewrites, which the endpoint needs to answer it quickly.

2026-11-20T05:14:42+00:00 · spoke-genelab · 7 rows logged

SPARQL (16 lines) 
PREFIX rdf: <http://www.w3.org/1999/02/22-rdf-syntax-ns#>
PREFIX kg: <https://purl.org/okn/frink/kg/spoke-genelab/schema/>
# Compact DE signature per contrast: human Entrez (ortholog for mouse; self for human) : log2FC ; adj_p<=0.05 & |log2FC|>=1
SELECT ?a ?dir (COUNT(DISTINCT ?h) AS ?n) (GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT CONCAT(?h, ":", STR(ROUND(?lfc*100)/100)); separator=";") AS ?genes) WHERE {
  GRAPH <https://purl.org/okn/frink/kg/spoke-genelab> {
    VALUES ?assay { <https://purl.org/okn/frink/kg/spoke-genelab/node/OSD-690-f82a89dc82f2903149d2d11cbd6a130d> <https://purl.org/okn/frink/kg/spoke-genelab/node/OSD-690-d89cbb20c4b7855f3f955e4adbb6515d> <https://purl.org/okn/frink/kg/spoke-genelab/node/OSD-214-0092f94d01682ca951bc130ab667111a> <https://purl.org/okn/frink/kg/spoke-genelab/node/OSD-467-4d3703d7504fd48caceedadb36799194> }
    ?st rdf:subject ?assay ;
        rdf:predicate kg:MEASURED_DIFFERENTIAL_EXPRESSION_ASmMG ; rdf:object ?gene ;
        kg:log2fc ?lfc ; kg:adj_p_value ?p .
    FILTER(?p <= 0.05 && ABS(?lfc) >= 1)
    ?gene kg:IS_ORTHOLOG_MGiG ?hgene .
    BIND(STRAFTER(STR(?hgene), "gene/") AS ?h)
    BIND(STRAFTER(STR(?assay), "node/") AS ?a)
    BIND(IF(?lfc > 0, "up", "down") AS ?dir)
  }
} GROUP BY ?a ?dir

q12 — rdkg: curated low-BMD gene set (genes of rare diseases with HP osteoporosis / osteopenia / reduced BMD)¶

2026-11-20T05:16:34+00:00 · rdkg · 940 rows logged

SPARQL (14 lines) 
PREFIX obo: <http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/>
PREFIX bl: <https://w3id.org/biolink/vocab/>
# rdkg curated (rare/Mendelian) low-bone-mass gene set: genes of rare MONDO diseases annotated with HP Osteoporosis / Osteopenia / Reduced bone mineral density
SELECT ?entrez (COUNT(DISTINCT ?d) AS ?nDiseases) WHERE {
  { SELECT DISTINCT ?d WHERE { GRAPH <https://purl.org/okn/frink/kg/rdkg> {
      VALUES ?hp { obo:HP_0000939 obo:HP_0000938 obo:HP_0004349 }
      ?d bl:has_phenotype ?hp .
      FILTER(STRSTARTS(STR(?d), "http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/MONDO_")) } } }
  GRAPH <https://purl.org/okn/frink/kg/rdkg> {
    { ?g bl:related_to ?d } UNION { ?d bl:genetic_association ?g }
    FILTER(STRSTARTS(STR(?g), "http://identifiers.org/ncbigene/"))
  }
  BIND(STRAFTER(STR(?g), "ncbigene/") AS ?entrez)
} GROUP BY ?entrez

q19 — rdkg -> babel -> prokn (DB2 skeleton): protein targets of rdkg osteoporosis drugs¶

2026-11-20T05:17:41+00:00 · rdkg, babel, prokn · 18 rows logged

SPARQL (19 lines) 
PREFIX rdf: <http://www.w3.org/1999/02/22-rdf-syntax-ns#>
PREFIX rdfs: <http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#>
# DB2 skeleton (rdkg DrugBank -> babel -> prokn ChEMBL compound) extended: protein targets + action of rdkg osteoporosis drugs
SELECT DISTINCT ?drugLabel ?sym ?action WHERE {
  { SELECT DISTINCT ?drug ?drugLabel ?pref WHERE {
      GRAPH <https://purl.org/okn/frink/kg/rdkg> {
        { ?d <https://w3id.org/biolink/vocab/subclass_of> <http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/MONDO_0005298> } UNION { VALUES ?d { <http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/MONDO_0005298> } }
        ?drug <https://w3id.org/biolink/vocab/treats> ?d ; a <https://w3id.org/biolink/vocab/Drug> ; <http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#label> ?drugLabel . }
      GRAPH <https://purl.org/okn/frink/kg/babel> { ?drug <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#exactMatch> ?pref } } }
  GRAPH <https://purl.org/okn/frink/kg/babel> { ?chembl <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#exactMatch> ?pref }
  FILTER(STRSTARTS(STR(?chembl),'http://identifiers.org/chembl.compound/'))
  BIND(IRI(CONCAT('https://www.ebi.ac.uk/chembl/explore/compound/',STRAFTER(STR(?chembl),'chembl.compound/'))) AS ?cpd)
  GRAPH <https://purl.org/okn/frink/kg/prokn> {
    ?cpd a <http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/NCIT_C43366> .
    ?st rdf:subject ?cpd ; rdf:predicate <https://w3id.org/biolink/vocab/directly_physically_interacts_with> ; rdf:object ?prot .
    OPTIONAL { ?st <http://purl.allotrope.org/ontologies/result#AFR_0003142> ?action }
    ?gene <http://semanticscience.org/resource/SIO_010078> ?prot ; rdfs:label ?sym .
  }
}

PREFIX bl: <https://w3id.org/biolink/vocab/>
# Enrichment n: per spaceflight contrast, DE genes (adj_p<=0.05,|log2FC|>=1; human Entrez = ortholog for mouse, self for human) that fall in the rdkg disease-gene universe (C6 Entrez join)
SELECT ?assay (COUNT(DISTINCT ?h) AS ?n_in_rdkg) WHERE {
  { SELECT DISTINCT ?assay ?h WHERE { GRAPH <https://purl.org/okn/frink/kg/spoke-genelab> {
      VALUES ?assay { <https://purl.org/okn/frink/kg/spoke-genelab/node/OSD-690-f82a89dc82f2903149d2d11cbd6a130d> <https://purl.org/okn/frink/kg/spoke-genelab/node/OSD-690-d89cbb20c4b7855f3f955e4adbb6515d> <https://purl.org/okn/frink/kg/spoke-genelab/node/OSD-546-7d689d4277a131607670c3e624202a44> }
      ?st rdf:subject ?assay ; rdf:predicate kg:MEASURED_DIFFERENTIAL_EXPRESSION_ASmMG ; rdf:object ?gene ; kg:log2fc ?lfc ; kg:adj_p_value ?p .
      FILTER(?p <= 0.05 && ABS(?lfc) >= 1)
      { ?gene kg:IS_ORTHOLOG_MGiG ?h } UNION { ?gene kg:taxonomy obo:NCBITaxon_9606 . BIND(?gene AS ?h) }
  } } }
  BIND(IRI(CONCAT("http://identifiers.org/ncbigene/", STRAFTER(STR(?h), "gene/"))) AS ?r)
  GRAPH <https://purl.org/okn/frink/kg/rdkg> { ?r a bl:Gene . FILTER EXISTS { { ?r bl:related_to ?d } UNION { ?d bl:related_to ?r } UNION { ?d bl:genetic_association ?r } } }
} GROUP BY ?assay

q23 — spoke-genelab x prokn: Reactome k (signature) and K (all prokn) per pathway¶

2026-11-20T05:20:01+00:00 · spoke-genelab, prokn · 183 rows logged

SPARQL (22 lines) 
PREFIX rdf: <http://www.w3.org/1999/02/22-rdf-syntax-ns#>
PREFIX obo: <http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/>
PREFIX rdfs: <http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#>
PREFIX kg: <https://purl.org/okn/frink/kg/spoke-genelab/schema/>
# Reactome over-representation (prokn gene->protein->participates_in->R-HSA pathway). Signatures = spaceflight DE (adj_p<=0.05,|log2FC|>=1) human genes, joined to prokn on HGNC symbol (rdfs:label). Returns k (signature genes in pathway) and K (all prokn genes in pathway); k>=4.
SELECT ?sigset ?pw (SAMPLE(?pl) AS ?label) (COUNT(DISTINCT ?sym) AS ?k) (SAMPLE(?K0) AS ?K) WHERE {
  { SELECT DISTINCT ?sigset ?sym WHERE { GRAPH <https://purl.org/okn/frink/kg/spoke-genelab> {
      VALUES (?assay ?sigset) { (<https://purl.org/okn/frink/kg/spoke-genelab/node/OSD-690-f82a89dc82f2903149d2d11cbd6a130d> "SF_BM") (<https://purl.org/okn/frink/kg/spoke-genelab/node/OSD-690-d89cbb20c4b7855f3f955e4adbb6515d> "SF_BM") (<https://purl.org/okn/frink/kg/spoke-genelab/node/OSD-546-7d689d4277a131607670c3e624202a44> "SF_hMSC_osteo") }
      ?st rdf:subject ?assay ; rdf:predicate kg:MEASURED_DIFFERENTIAL_EXPRESSION_ASmMG ; rdf:object ?gene ; kg:log2fc ?lfc ; kg:adj_p_value ?p .
      FILTER(?p <= 0.05 && ABS(?lfc) >= 1)
      { ?gene kg:IS_ORTHOLOG_MGiG ?h } UNION { ?gene kg:taxonomy obo:NCBITaxon_9606 . BIND(?gene AS ?h) }
      ?h kg:symbol ?sym . } } }
  GRAPH <https://purl.org/okn/frink/kg/prokn> {
    ?g rdfs:label ?sym ; <http://semanticscience.org/resource/SIO_010078> ?prot .
    ?prot <https://w3id.org/biolink/vocab/participates_in> ?pw .
    ?pw a <http://purl.uniprot.org/core/Pathway> . FILTER(CONTAINS(STR(?pw), "R-HSA"))
    OPTIONAL { ?pw rdfs:label ?pl }
  }
  { SELECT ?pw (COUNT(DISTINCT ?g2) AS ?K0) WHERE { GRAPH <https://purl.org/okn/frink/kg/prokn> {
      ?g2 <http://semanticscience.org/resource/SIO_010078> ?p2 . ?p2 <https://w3id.org/biolink/vocab/participates_in> ?pw .
      ?pw a <http://purl.uniprot.org/core/Pathway> . FILTER(CONTAINS(STR(?pw), "R-HSA")) } } GROUP BY ?pw }
} GROUP BY ?sigset ?pw HAVING (COUNT(DISTINCT ?sym) >= 4)

PREFIX rdf: <http://www.w3.org/1999/02/22-rdf-syntax-ns#>
PREFIX obo: <http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/>

# Reactome enrichment backgrounds: n = signature genes with >=1 prokn R-HSA pathway (per signature); N = all prokn genes with >=1 R-HSA pathway (sigset "ALL_prokn")

        ?st rdf:subject ?assay ; rdf:predicate kg:MEASURED_DIFFERENTIAL_EXPRESSION_ASmMG ; rdf:object ?gene ; kg:log2fc ?lfc ; kg:adj_p_value ?p .
        FILTER(?p <= 0.05 && ABS(?lfc) >= 1)
        { ?gene kg:IS_ORTHOLOG_MGiG ?h } UNION { ?gene kg:taxonomy obo:NCBITaxon_9606 . BIND(?gene AS ?h) }
        ?h kg:symbol ?sym . } } }
    GRAPH <https://purl.org/okn/frink/kg/prokn> { ?g rdfs:label ?sym ; <http://semanticscience.org/resource/SIO_010078> ?prot . ?prot <https://w3id.org/biolink/vocab/participates_in> ?pw . ?pw a <http://purl.uniprot.org/core/Pathway> . FILTER(CONTAINS(STR(?pw), "R-HSA")) }
  } UNION {
    GRAPH <https://purl.org/okn/frink/kg/prokn> { ?g <http://semanticscience.org/resource/SIO_010078> ?prot . ?prot <https://w3id.org/biolink/vocab/participates_in> ?pw . ?pw a <http://purl.uniprot.org/core/Pathway> . FILTER(CONTAINS(STR(?pw), "R-HSA")) }
    BIND("ALL_prokn" AS ?sigset)
  }
} GROUP BY ?sigset

q25 — spoke-genelab x prokn: GO-BP k and K per term (GO-NOT removed)¶

2026-11-20T05:20:31+00:00 · spoke-genelab, prokn, ubergraph · 394 rows logged

SPARQL (23 lines) 
PREFIX rdf: <http://www.w3.org/1999/02/22-rdf-syntax-ns#>
PREFIX obo: <http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/>
PREFIX rdfs: <http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#>
PREFIX kg: <https://purl.org/okn/frink/kg/spoke-genelab/schema/>
# GO Biological Process over-representation (prokn gene->protein->biolink:actively_involved_in->GO; reified statements, GO NOT-qualified (NegativePropertyAssertion) statements removed). k>=5, 10<=K<=500.
SELECT ?sigset ?go (SAMPLE(?gl) AS ?label) (COUNT(DISTINCT ?sym) AS ?k) (SAMPLE(?K0) AS ?K) WHERE {
  { SELECT DISTINCT ?sigset ?sym WHERE { GRAPH <https://purl.org/okn/frink/kg/spoke-genelab> {
      VALUES (?assay ?sigset) { (<https://purl.org/okn/frink/kg/spoke-genelab/node/OSD-690-f82a89dc82f2903149d2d11cbd6a130d> "SF_BM") (<https://purl.org/okn/frink/kg/spoke-genelab/node/OSD-690-d89cbb20c4b7855f3f955e4adbb6515d> "SF_BM") (<https://purl.org/okn/frink/kg/spoke-genelab/node/OSD-546-7d689d4277a131607670c3e624202a44> "SF_hMSC_osteo") }
      ?st rdf:subject ?assay ; rdf:predicate kg:MEASURED_DIFFERENTIAL_EXPRESSION_ASmMG ; rdf:object ?gene ; kg:log2fc ?lfc ; kg:adj_p_value ?p .
      FILTER(?p <= 0.05 && ABS(?lfc) >= 1)
      { ?gene kg:IS_ORTHOLOG_MGiG ?h } UNION { ?gene kg:taxonomy obo:NCBITaxon_9606 . BIND(?gene AS ?h) }
      ?h kg:symbol ?sym . } } }
  GRAPH <https://purl.org/okn/frink/kg/prokn> {
    ?g rdfs:label ?sym ; <http://semanticscience.org/resource/SIO_010078> ?prot .
    ?s1 rdf:subject ?prot ; rdf:predicate <https://w3id.org/biolink/vocab/actively_involved_in> ; rdf:object ?go .
    MINUS { ?s1 rdf:type <https://www.w3.org/2002/07/owl#NegativePropertyAssertion> }
  }
  { SELECT ?go (COUNT(DISTINCT ?g2) AS ?K0) WHERE { GRAPH <https://purl.org/okn/frink/kg/prokn> {
      ?g2 <http://semanticscience.org/resource/SIO_010078> ?p2 .
      ?s2 rdf:subject ?p2 ; rdf:predicate <https://w3id.org/biolink/vocab/actively_involved_in> ; rdf:object ?go .
      MINUS { ?s2 rdf:type <https://www.w3.org/2002/07/owl#NegativePropertyAssertion> } } } GROUP BY ?go HAVING (COUNT(DISTINCT ?g2) >= 10 && COUNT(DISTINCT ?g2) <= 500) }
  OPTIONAL { GRAPH <https://purl.org/okn/frink/kg/ubergraph> { ?go rdfs:label ?gl } }
} GROUP BY ?sigset ?go HAVING (COUNT(DISTINCT ?sym) >= 5)

PREFIX obo: <http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/>

PREFIX bl: <https://w3id.org/biolink/vocab/>
# rdkg disease->phenotype (forward edges only) for osteoporosis (MONDO_0005298) and its MONDO descendants; HP label from ubergraph
SELECT ?hp (SAMPLE(?hl) AS ?label) (COUNT(DISTINCT ?d) AS ?nDiseases) WHERE {
  GRAPH <https://purl.org/okn/frink/kg/rdkg> {
    { ?d bl:subclass_of obo:MONDO_0005298 } UNION { VALUES ?d { obo:MONDO_0005298 } }
    FILTER(STRSTARTS(STR(?d), "http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/MONDO_"))
    ?d bl:has_phenotype ?hp . FILTER(STRSTARTS(STR(?hp), "http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/HP_"))
  }
  OPTIONAL { GRAPH <https://purl.org/okn/frink/kg/ubergraph> { ?hp rdfs:label ?hl } }
} GROUP BY ?hp HAVING (COUNT(DISTINCT ?d) >= 2)

Analysis¶

Question and approach¶

What genes, pathways, biomarkers and drug targets explain spaceflight-induced bone loss, and how do actual spaceflight, terrestrial unloading analogs and human bone disorders agree? The approach takes vetted spaceflight-vs-ground and hindlimb-unloading contrasts from spoke-genelab, projects mouse genes to human orthologs, and tests the resulting signatures against curated rare low-BMD disease genes (rdkg) and GWAS-style BMD/osteoporosis genes (digcfdekg) on Entrez. Pathway programmes come from prokn (GO-BP and Reactome, joined on HGNC symbol), drugs from rdkg treats bridged through babel to prokn targets, and biomarkers / phenotypes from biomarkerkg and rdkg. Genes are integrated into an evidence score and A/B/C tiers, then synthesised into a mechanistic map. Everything is hypothesis generation.

Replicator specification¶

  • Contrasts (spoke-genelab v0.0.2; get_valid_contrasts rule: Space Flight arm 1 vs Ground Control arm 2, same covariates and material): OSD-690-f82a89dc (marrow, WT), OSD-690-d89cbb20 (marrow, Nrf2-KO), OSD-546-7d689d42 (hMSC, osteogenic medium). Analogs (factor arms, no factor_space): OSD-467-4d3703d7 (cortical bone, HLU vs normal loading), OSD-214-0092f94d (marrow, HLU vs loaded, no CpG / tetanus-toxoid). Log2FC > 0 = up in arm 1 (flight / unloaded).
  • DE call: reified MEASURED_DIFFERENTIAL_EXPRESSION_ASmMG, adj_p_value <= 0.05 and |log2fc| >= 1. Mouse -> human via IS_ORTHOLOG_MGiG; human genes (taxonomy 9606) map to themselves. Many-to-one collisions keep the largest |log2FC| (q08, q09).
  • Bone gene sets: rdkg MONDO diseases with has_phenotype HP_0000939 / HP_0000938 / HP_0004349, genes via related_to (either direction) or genetic_association (q12; universe N = rdkg genes with any disease link, q17). digcfdekg geneToTrait for 10 BMD / osteoporosis traits (q15; core = >= 3 traits; universe N = numeric-Entrez genes with any trait, q16). n = signature genes inside each universe, counted server-side (q20, q22). q21 is superseded by q22.
  • Pathways: prokn gene SIO_010078 -> protein -> actively_involved_in (GO-BP, reified, NegativePropertyAssertion removed; 10 <= K <= 500, k >= 5) or participates_in R-HSA (k >= 4). Join to spoke-genelab on human symbol = prokn rdfs:label. Hypergeometric; BH-FDR within family x signature over returned terms.
  • Drugs: rdkg treats on MONDO_0005298 + subclass_of descendants (q18); DB2 skeleton rdkg DrugBank -> babel clique -> ChEMBL -> prokn compound -> directly_physically_interacts_with protein -> gene (q19). Candidate druggability: prokn compound -> protein for the 446 bone-linked DE genes (q29), named phase >= 3 agents (q30).
  • Tiers: A = (rdkg and >= 3 digcfdekg traits) or (>= 2 flight contrasts and (rdkg or >= 3 traits)); B = rdkg or >= 3 traits, or >= 2 contrasts with any trait; C = otherwise. Score = recurrence ((n_sf-1)/2) + effect (max|log2FC|/3, cap 1) + rdkg (0/1) + digcfdekg (traits/5, cap 1) + drug (1 osteoporosis-drug target, 0.75 phase 4, 0.5 phase 3).
  • Modules (map): each Tier-A gene assigned to the module with most distinct GO-BP annotations among the listed enriched terms (q31); ties to the earlier module; <= 7 genes per module.
  • Verified quantities: DE genes 202 / 297 / 1463 (flight), 7 / 3 (HLU); 446 bone-linked flight DE genes; 40 / 212 / 194 genes in tiers A / B / C.
  • Limitations: three flight contrasts only (no flown bone tissue); near-empty HLU signatures; ortholog projection; symbol string join to prokn; FDR over returned terms only.

Why this step: load the analysis helpers (analysis.py), the report figure style (okn_figstyle.py, from the okn-report-style skill) and the mechanistic-map renderer (mechanistic_map.py, from the okn-bioanalysis skill).

In [33]:
import os, json
import numpy as np, pandas as pd, matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import analysis as A
import okn_figstyle as F
from mechanistic_map import render_mechanistic_map
F.apply_style()
os.makedirs("figures", exist_ok=True)

Why this step: turn the compact signature queries (q08, q09) into one long table and count DE genes per contrast and direction — the inventory in report §3.

In [34]:
# Inventory of the five contrasts: DE genes (adj_p <= 0.05, |log2FC| >= 1; human Entrez, ortholog-projected for mouse)
sig = A.signatures(data)
inventory = (sig.assign(direction=np.where(sig.lfc > 0, "up", "down"))
               .pivot_table(index="contrast", columns="direction", values="entrez", aggfunc="nunique", fill_value=0))
inventory["total"] = inventory.sum(axis=1)
inventory = inventory.loc[["SF_BM_WT", "SF_BM_Nrf2KO", "SF_hMSC_osteo", "HLU_BM", "HLU_cortical"]]
inventory

Why this step: Figure 1 shows how much signal each contrast carries and which signatures concentrate bone-disorder genes.

In [38]:
Python (33 lines) 
# Figure 1 — design overview: (A) DE inventory per contrast, (B) bone-gene-set enrichment
fig, (ax1, ax2) = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(12.5, 4.6), gridspec_kw={"width_ratios": [1, 1.35]})
labels = {"SF_BM_WT": "Flight BM (WT)", "SF_BM_Nrf2KO": "Flight BM (Nrf2-KO)", "SF_hMSC_osteo": "Flight hMSC osteogenic",
          "HLU_BM": "HLU BM (analog)", "HLU_cortical": "HLU cortical bone (analog)"}
inv = inventory.copy()
y = np.arange(len(inv))
ax1.barh(y, -inv["down"], color=F.DOWN, label="down")
ax1.barh(y, inv["up"], color=F.UP, label="up")
ax1.set_yticks(y); ax1.set_yticklabels([labels[c] for c in inv.index]); ax1.invert_yaxis()
ax1.set_xscale("symlog", linthresh=10)
ax1.axvline(0, color="#444", lw=0.8)
for i, (u, d) in enumerate(zip(inv["up"], inv["down"])):
    ax1.text(u * 1.15 + 1, i, str(u), va="center", fontsize=8); ax1.text(-d * 1.15 - 1, i, str(d), va="center", ha="right", fontsize=8)
ax1.set_xlim(-9000, 6000)
ax1.set_xlabel("DE genes (symlog; left = down, right = up)")
F.panel_title(ax1, "A", "DE genes per contrast")
F.legend_outside(ax1, where="below", ncol=2)
b = bone.copy()
b["lab"] = b.contrast.map(labels) + " · " + b.gene_set.str.replace("genes ", "").str.replace("digcfdekg ", "dig ")
b = b.sort_values(["contrast", "gene_set"])
colors = {"rdkg": "#0072B2", "digcfdekg": "#E69F00"}
yy = np.arange(len(b))
ax2.barh(yy, b.fold, color=[colors[s] for s in b.supplier])
ax2.axvline(1, color="#444", ls="--", lw=0.8)
ax2.set_yticks(yy); ax2.set_yticklabels(b.lab, fontsize=8); ax2.invert_yaxis()
for i, (f, q, k, K) in enumerate(zip(b.fold, b.fdr, b.k, b.K)):
    ax2.text(f + 0.03, i, f"{k}/{K}  FDR {q:.1e}" if q < 0.05 else f"{k}/{K}  ns", va="center", fontsize=7.5)
ax2.set_xlim(0, b.fold.max() * 1.6)
ax2.set_xlabel("fold enrichment (observed / expected)")
F.panel_title(ax2, "B", "Bone gene-set enrichment")
import matplotlib.patches as mp
F.legend_outside(ax2, [mp.Patch(color=c) for c in colors.values()], list(colors), where="below", ncol=2, title="supplier")
F.finalize(fig, 1, "figures/fig1_design_inventory_enrichment.png")

Why this step: Figure 3 names the programmes behind the signatures, coloured by an analyst-assigned theme so the ER/secretory, bone/ECM, growth-factor, inflammatory and vascular groups are visible.

In [40]:
Python (24 lines) 
# Figure 3 — functional enrichment: (A) GO-BP and (B) Reactome for the osteogenic hMSC flight signature; (C) GO-BP for flight bone marrow
theme_kw = [("ER/secretory stress", ["endoplasmic", "ERAD", "unfolded", "COPII", "Cargo", "XBP1", "ERQC", "Golgi", "glycosylation", "vesicle"]),
            ("Bone/ECM", ["osteoblast", "collagen", "skeletal", "bone", "elastic", "ECM", "matrix", "Laminin", "proteoglycan", "BMP", "fat cell", "basement"]),
            ("Growth-factor / TGF-β", ["transforming", "TGF", "PDGF", "IGF", "MET ", "SMAD"]),
            ("Inflammation / immune", ["lipopolysaccharide", "chemotaxis", "Interleukin", "inflammatory", "immune", "Basigin", "tumor necrosis"]),
            ("Vascular / hypoxia", ["angiogenesis", "hypoxia", "endothelial", "Smooth Muscle", "wound"])]
tcol = {"ER/secretory stress": "#CC79A7", "Bone/ECM": "#0072B2", "Growth-factor / TGF-β": "#009E73",
        "Inflammation / immune": "#D55E00", "Vascular / hypoxia": "#E69F00", "other": "#999999"}
def theme(l):
    for t, kws in theme_kw:
        if any(k.lower() in l.lower() for k in kws): return t
    return "other"
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(17, 6.8), gridspec_kw={"width_ratios": [1, 1, 0.85]})
for ax, (fam, sigset, letter, ttl) in zip(axes, [("GO-BP", "SF_hMSC_osteo", "A", "GO-BP · flight hMSC osteogenic"),
                                               ("Reactome", "SF_hMSC_osteo", "B", "Reactome · flight hMSC osteogenic"),
                                               ("GO-BP", "SF_BM", "C", "GO-BP · flight bone marrow (WT ∪ KO)")]):
    x = terms[(terms.family == fam) & (terms.signature == sigset) & (terms.fdr < 0.05)].sort_values("p").head(15)
    labs = [l if len(l) <= 46 else l[:44] + "…" for l in x.label]
    th = [theme(l) for l in x.label]
    F.ranked_barh(ax, labs, list(-np.log10(x.fdr)), themes=th, theme_colors=tcol,
                  annots=[f"{f:.1f}× ({k}/{K})" for f, k, K in zip(x.fold, x.k, x.K)], xlabel="−log10(FDR)")
    F.panel_title(ax, letter, ttl)
F.theme_legend(axes[1], {k: v for k, v in tcol.items()}, where="below", title="theme")
F.finalize(fig, 3, "figures/fig3_go_reactome.png")

Python (22 lines) 
# Figure 5 — mechanistic map (anchor -> module -> Tier-A gene -> phase>=3 agent on that gene)
mods = A.module_membership(data, tiers)
dr = A.druggability(data)
drugs = {}
for m, genes in mods.items():
    ds = []
    for g in genes:
        if g in dr["names"]:
            ds += [f"{n.split(' (')[0]} → {g}" for n in dr["names"][g].split("; ")[:1]]
    if ds: drugs[m] = ds[:3]
render_mechanistic_map(
    anchor="Spaceflight\nbone loss", modules=mods, drugs=drugs,
    out_path="figures/fig5_mechanistic_map.png",
    title="Spaceflight bone loss: module → Tier-A gene → agent map (entities retrieved from OKN graphs)",
    gene_legend="Tier-A gene (spoke-genelab DE + rdkg/digcfdekg)", module_legend="Module (GO-BP synthesis, prokn)",
    drug_legend="Phase ≥3 agent acting on that gene (prokn)", anchor_kind="Condition")
# save it through the report figure style (same pixels: figure size = image size at 150 dpi), which also shows it here

Figure 5. Mechanistic map of spaceflight bone loss. Anchor (star) → modules (squares) → Tier-A genes (circles) → phase ≥3 agents acting on those genes (triangles). Modules are an analyst synthesis: each Tier-A gene is placed in the theme where it carries the most prokn GO-BP annotations among the enriched bone-relevant terms (q31; ties to the earlier module; up to seven genes per module by score). Agents are drawn only where a prokn compound → protein edge ties them to a gene in that module. Provenance: spoke-genelab, rdkg, digcfdekg (genes); prokn (modules, agents).

Conclusions¶

  • The osteogenic hMSC flight signature is enriched for bone-mass genes: 113 of its genes carry >= 3 digcfdekg BMD/osteoporosis traits (2.1x, FDR 1.4e-13) and 136 are rdkg rare low-BMD disease genes (1.58x, FDR 4.0e-08); flight bone-marrow signatures show no such enrichment in the curated set.
  • ALPL is the only gene down in all three flight contrasts; 9 of the 10 genes DE in all three move in opposite directions in marrow and hMSC (chemokines up in marrow, down in hMSC).
  • GO-BP (63 terms) and Reactome (41 terms) at FDR < 0.05 in the hMSC signature centre on ER-to-Golgi secretion, glycosylation, UPR (effectors down), collagen / elastic fibres and osteoblast differentiation.
  • 446 bone-linked flight DE genes yield 40 Tier-A genes (IL6, ENG, LMNA, FGFR2, RUNX2, COL1A1, DKK1, TNFRSF11B, ALPL, ...); none of the 8 targets of rdkg's osteoporosis drugs is DE, but their pathway neighbours are.
  • 28 bone-linked DE genes are hit by phase >= 3 compounds; read with direction, CTSK (up; odanacatib) is the most coherent lead, while IL6 and PTGS2 are down in flight.

The federation supports an osteoblast / Wnt-antagonist / matrix-secretion mechanism for spaceflight bone loss with countermeasures acting through adjacent pathways; the main limitation is that only three bone-relevant flight contrasts exist and the unloading analogs in the graph are nearly empty.

Verify against the live graphs¶

verify_all() re-runs every query and compares it with the logged result. status is ok, drift (the row count changed), changed (the same number of rows, different values) or an error, and redeployed names each graph whose release differs from the one in the header. A difference usually means the graph was redeployed since the study ran, not that the analysis is wrong.

verify_all()
